sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record ekii1241 and bibliography (langdoc.bib?language=ekii1241)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: 2 refs total (Blench Atlas 1999 and 2020 editions, hhtype overview); 0 descriptive refs; MED = wordlist_or_less; classified Efikic > Unclassified Efikic.
One-line stub ('Eki is an Ibibio-Efik language of Nigeria', Akwa Ibom State, 5,000 speakers cited 1992); sole reference Ethnologue 25; nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. 2020 edition. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation / McDonald Institute for Archaeological Research.
sources.note: Entry 112. Eki, printed p.27 (PDF p.55): '3. Cross River State / 4. 5000 plus (1988) / 5. Benue-Congo: Cross River: Delta-Cross: Lower Cross: (no data) - dialect of Efik? / Refs. Overview: Connell (1991)'. No linguistic data; nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 1994. The Lower Cross languages: a prolegomena to the classification of the Cross River languages. Journal of West African Languages 24(1): 3-46.
sources.note: Eki does not appear in the scanned pp.3-16 (sample list, inventories). Sec. 3.3 p.10: all LC languages have two tones H/L plus contrastive downstep; sec. 5 p.12: interaction of tone with 'phrasal stress' uninvestigated except Faraclas 1984b for Obolo. No word-stress statement, no Eki data.

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce A. 1991. Phonetic aspects of the Lower Cross languages and their implications for sound change. PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh (vol. 1). hdl:1842/19642; CORE mirror https://core.ac.uk/download/
sources.note: Eki is NOT in the 19-language sample: p.7 (PDF p.21) 'Eki, Idere, and Ito are said to be distinct Lower Cross varieties, but to date no data have been collected for these'. Group-level only: all LC languages 'two-toned, terraced level languages' (p.47); 'difficult to find any true evidence for stress' in Efik beyond likely phrasal/compound-juncture stress (pp.54-55, fn.32); LC called 'a non-stress language' (fn.34 p.56). No word-stress rule for any LC language.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2025. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 28th ed. Entry: Eki [eki].

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. n.d. Lower Cross Wordlist. Unpublished ms., 91 pp. (Glottolog ref 101094, listed for other LC languages); and any post-1991 Connell field data on Eki/Idere.

sources.note: Connell 1991 p.7 says no Eki data had been collected 'to date'; if later Lower Cross survey work by Connell reached Eki, tone-marked forms would show whether it patterns with Efik (two tones + downstep, no word stress).

sources.citation: Faraclas, Nicholas. 1989. Cross River. In John Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo Languages, 377-399. Lanham: University Press of America.

sources.citation: Cook, Thomas L. 1985. An integrated phonology of Efik, vol. 1. PhD dissertation, Leiden University; and Ward, Ida C. 1933. The phonetic and tonal structure of Efik. Cambridge: Heffer.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: If Eki is an Efik dialect (Blench 2020), the Efik phonologies are the nearest primary descriptions of its prosody (Ward posits verb-root stress; Cook/Connell treat Efik as tonal without word stress).
